patch.value: Secret guard: keep lexer distrust after a declined quote local to the affected segment, and decode adjacent Python literals before judging a value

pm-gh1781 made the string lexer conservative: once a line declines a quote of a kind (a quote right after a word character), no later string of that kind on the line ends a value, because a shell segment opened there shifts every later boundary and a cut there hid literals main reported. The rule over-reaches in valid structured text: a plain YAML flow scalar holding a prose apostrophe disables every later single-quoted boundary on its line, and a shell word with a joined double-quoted segment does the same for double quotes, so a later member holding only a bare reference is judged as literal text; main reported nothing for both. Separately, the shell-word text reading of a single-quoted value joins Python adjacent literals but keeps a hex escape between them literal, so a value Python decodes to exactly one bare reference is reported. Found by the Codex round 5 review of PR #1789; both are false positives, no lost finding.

After a declined quote, trust resumes at a boundary that resolves the ambiguity (a confirmed scalar, flow-mapping or shell-word boundary), so a later member's bare reference is clean while the shell desync lines from pm-gh1781 stay reported; Adjacent Python string literals are decoded and joined before the value is judged in Python expression context; the backslash-keeping join stays for shell words; The pm-gh1781 corpus differential shows no lost finding
A bare reference in a structured member is a placeholder however the line began
A prose apostrophe or a joined shell segment earlier on the line makes a later bare reference a finding

value.text: Also in scope, from Greptile and Codex round 5 on PR #1789: a Python string that escapes an apostrophe (an escaped-apostrophe bytes or raw string, or an unprefixed one after an assignment) reads as a shell close under the per-line lexer, so a later dict member on its line keeps the conservative reading and a bare reference there is reported. Two narrower exceptions (treating the quote that ends the word after an escaped apostrophe as Python's closer, and judging a prefixed string's escapes by the context before its prefix) were tried and reverted on PR #1789, because each let a shell line hide a literal that main reports (both lines are spec cases). A fix needs a signal that separates Python from shell context beyond one quote's neighbourhood.
